title: Nilo-Saharan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Nilo-Saharan languages are a proposed linguistic family consisting of around 210 Native African languages spoken by somewhere around 70 million speakers, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia, north of where the two tributaries of the Nile meet.

title: Nyangatom | Ethnologue Free
text: Nyangatom is a stable indigenous language of Ethiopia. It belongs to the Nilo-Saharan language family.

title: Nyangatom Tribe | Destiny Ethiopia Tours - We Make Memories!
text: Also known as Bume, the Nyangatom belong to the Nilo-Saharan linguistic group. They live throughout the eastern part of the Lower Omo Valley and the Kibish Basin, even into Sudan. Closely related to the Topossa people of Sudan, they shun conflict with these neighbours.

title: Nyangatom - nnj (Nilo-Saharan) - PeopleGroups.org
text: Nyangatom (nnj) is part of the Nilo-Saharan family and Nilo-Saharan, Satellite-Core, Core, Eastern Sudanic, Southern (n languages), Nilotic, Eastern, Lotuxo-Teso, Teso-Turkana, Turkana class.

title: BBC - Tribe - Nyangatom
text: Linguistically, the Nyangatom have most in common with the Turkana and the Mursi. These three tribes speak Nilo-Saharan languages, whereas other tribes in the region (Karo, Hamar and Dassanesh) speak Afro-Asiatic languages.

title: Nyangatom tribe of Omo Valley - My Ethiopia Tours
text: Nyangatom is one of the tribes of Ethiopia's Lower Omo Valley.The Nyangatom people speak the Nyangatom language, which belongs to the Eastern Nilotic branch of the Nilo-Saharan language family.

title: AfricaBib | The Nyangatom: an outline of their ecology and social...
text: The 5000 agro-pastoral Nyangatom inhabit a part of the Lower Omo Valley in Ethiopia and adjacent western lowlands and mountain piedmonts in Sudan.Linguistically, they are a branch of the Nilotic sub-family, within the East Sudanic family of the wider Nilo-Saharan phylum.
